thread:
sasha: Seeing a bunch of GPU nodes go NotReady + pods evicted after yesterday's kernel rollout in eu-west. Only GPU pool affected. Possible device plugin failure during boot.

mike: ugh, any logs? which kernel version rolled?

sasha: kernel 6.1.34 -> 6.1.40 on the batch-gpu nodes. Here's kubelet/daemonset symptom: device-plugin starts, advertises 0 GPUs, then later driver modules show up. pods get scheduled -> OOM/evicted.

elaine: can you paste device-plugin logs and dmesg snippet? might be nvidia-uvm or nvidia-modeset ordering.

sasha: sure. short log:
```
Nov 12 06:12:03 node-gtx daemon[device-plugin]: starting device plugin
Nov 12 06:12:03 node-gtx daemon[device-plugin]: advertise: 0 devices
Nov 12 06:12:10 node-gtx kernel: nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
Nov 12 06:12:11 node-gtx kernel: nvidia: probe success
Nov 12 06:12:12 node-gtx daemon[device-plugin]: got 4 devices, updating advertise
```
pods scheduled in the 9s window got evicted because kubelet saw zero allocatable originally.

ben: that looks like module autoload happens after device-plugin startup. On our nodes the GPU operator updates drivers as a DKMS package which can finish later. We used to rely on modprobe order being early.

mike: Could be systemd unit ordering change in the new kernel packaging. If the driver module loads after kubelet registers resources, kubelet won't retroactively reconcile allocatable unless device-plugin triggers a resource update. Does our device-plugin have a restart-on-change hook?

elaine: currently gpu-operator's device-plugin container doesn't wait for /dev/nvidia0, it just starts. We can add an initContainer that polls for device nodes or for `nvidia-smi` succeeding. Quick mitigate: restart the daemonset after nodes booted: `kubectl rollout restart ds nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset -n gpu-system` — will cause re-advertise.

sasha: did that and it fixed the remaining nodes. But want a long term fix before next kernel batch.

ben: proposals: 1) patch our device-plugin DaemonSet to add `initContainers` that wait for modules: `until ls /dev/nvidia[0-9]*; do sleep 1; done` 2) add a node-level systemd unit that ensures nvidia modules load before kubelet (WantedBy=kubelet.service) 3) increase kubelet's eviction scheduling window? (risky)

mike: +1 for initContainer in device-plugin; less invasive. Also we should make the operator restart device-plugin only after driver install completes (driver helm/chart has a post-install hook). Might be a race introduced by the operator's driver upgrade flow.

elaine: I'll open a PR to gpu-operator to add the initContainer wait and to make the driver-hook create a configmap `driver-ready` that the device-plugin can wait on. Also add a preflight check in our cluster-roll script to detect kernel+dkms combos that take >5s to finish.

sasha: filing a postmortem aside: nodes impacted: eu-west-gpu-{03,07,09} — about 12 pods evicted, 4 alert pages. Cost/time ~1.2h remediation. Adding it to incident tracker.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2023-4823 (GPU node driver race) — linked to runbook gpu-driver-race.md

mike: for immediate ops doc: run `kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu -o wide` then `kubectl rollout restart ds nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset -n gpu-system` after node reboots. Add note to kernel rollout playbook.

ben: small note: keep an eye on NCCL errors after restart; if kernel ABI changes, some user pods show CC errors requiring driver re-install.

elaine: PR opened: https://git.company/repo/gpu-operator/pull/1423 — includes initContainer + probe script. I'll schedule a canary release to staging env first.

sasha: thanks all, marking this resolved for now. :thumbsup:
